A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TimeRecipe research. Their main text, equations, figure, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original forecasting experiments, module-property correlation analyses, and model-selection evaluations, with extensive numerical results in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds Environment and Security model-selection evaluations in Appendix C.2.

M1.justification: The canonical architecture, preprocessing operations, embedding alternatives, fusion configurations, and LightGBM-based architecture selector are retained. Expanded model mappings and scope explanations do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: The toolkit evaluation retains ETTh1_24_M and Social_12_S and adds univariate Environment_48_S and Security_12_S cases (Table 5). Section 4.2 describes an expansion from one to three out-of-distribution cases, although the added series are sparsely described. Core LTSF, PEMS, and M4 coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: The matched ETTh1 and Social comparisons retain PatchTST and the exhaustive-search reference. DLinear, already included in v1, supplies the existing-best reference on the added tasks. PAttn and Autoformer are newly listed as covered configurations in Table 1, without establishing additions to the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation design retains the forecasting definitions, error metrics, averaged-rank scoring, and top-three selector comparison. The added tasks use this same comparison structure; no revised splits, preprocessing, training budgets, model sizes, or testing procedures are documented.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix C.2 extend the selector's out-of-distribution transfer case studies from Social alone to Environment and Security. These test whether selected configurations remain competitive on additional unseen series. The module-property correlation analysis is unchanged; Table 2 largely redisplays it.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging four random seeds and testing module-property associations. V2 additionally reports a standard deviation of 2.88% and t-test p-value of 0.0069 for the existing 5.4% average error reduction (Section 4.1.1). This adds uncertainty and significance reporting without establishing additional runs.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds Environment and Security results; for example, Environment selection 3 achieves MSE 0.2920 versus DLinear's 0.2950. Original ETTh1/Social entries and appendix ranking tables remain unchanged. Several qualitative summaries are corrected, including patch embeddings favoring high rather than low trend, consistent with the retained appendix evidence.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, Equations 1–9, and dataset-property Algorithms 1–6 retain their mathematical content. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the contributions of module-level benchmarking, over 10,000 experiments, configurations outperforming existing methods, data-dependent module effectiveness, and a training-free architecture-selection toolkit.

C2.justification: Section 2.4 adds reasons for excluding designs, including combinatorial growth and coupling between pretrained components. Section 4.1.2 adds explanations involving normalization under distribution shift and RNN error accumulation, and highlights the different decomposition–shifting relationships in univariate and multivariate settings. Appendix D's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 1 adds explicit configuration mappings for PAttn and Autoformer, while Remark 2 specifies TimeMixer's module combination and omitted augmentation. These expand configuration documentation. The implementation library, V100 hardware, and code, data, and results access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Remark 3 explains the relationship between supervised modular benchmarking and foundation or prompt-based approaches, adding a TabPFN citation. CAPE and the invariant-learning forecasting paper disappear from the references. Most related-work discussion is retained; publication updates and duplicate bibliographic variants are not new research coverage.

P1.justification: Most prose and section order remain intact. Local revisions expand Section 2.4, rewrite the module-effectiveness discussion, add Appendix C.2, and remove the separate Section 3.4 heading while retaining its content. Citations switch from numbered to author-year style.

P2.justification: V2 adds the recommendation summary in Table 2, revises Table 1's rows and removes its venue column, and splits v1's model-selection table between Table 3 and expanded Appendix Table 5. Figure 1 and ranking-table structures are retained. The template changes headers, title/author arrangement, and float placement.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly strengthens selector-transfer evidence with two additional cases, quantifies uncertainty for the retained aggregate advantage, and clarifies scope and several recommendations. These benefits are limited by sparse descriptions of the added series and remaining reporting inconsistencies: Tables 2 and 4 disagree about normalization versus correlation, and Table 5 prints a Security MAE difference of −0.4% where its displayed values imply approximately −4.1%.
